about.title: About
about.lead: What Limpyrid is and how it keeps your files safe.
about.description: Limpyrid shows what fills your disk and cleans the development caches and folders that rebuild themselves, on Windows.
about.protects.1: Nothing is deleted without your confirmation, and the confirmation lists every folder and its size.
about.protects.2: Drive roots, Windows, Program Files, ProgramData and your user folder are blocked: no action deletes them.
about.protects.3: Worktrees with uncommitted changes, commits outside any branch or recent activity are shown but cannot be removed.
about.protects.4: In temporary folders, only what has not changed within the minimum age you choose is deleted.
about.doesNot.1: It sends no data anywhere: everything happens on this computer.
about.doesNot.2: It does not delete your models, WSL disks or app data: those categories are for information only.
about.doesNot.3: It does not follow symbolic links when deleting: it removes the link, never its target.

cat.temp-user.effect: Deletes your user temporary files that have not changed in recent days; files in use are skipped. Usually you will not notice anything: a program may take a little longer to open or lose something it left there from an earlier session. Windows and your programs create again what they need.
cat.temp-windows.effect: Deletes system temporary files that have not changed in recent days; files in use are skipped. Usually you will not notice anything. Windows and installers create again what they need.
cat.npm.effect: Deletes the packages npm kept in its cache; your projects and their node_modules are not touched. The next npm install downloads whatever is missing again, so it needs a connection and takes longer.
cat.pnpm.effect: Deletes the store where pnpm keeps one copy of each package; existing node_modules keep working. The next pnpm install downloads whatever is missing again, with a connection and more time. If your projects link these files, the space actually recovered will be less than shown.
cat.yarn.effect: Deletes the global Yarn cache (version 2 or later). Projects that use Plug'n'Play read their packages straight from this cache and will not start until you run yarn install in each of them, which downloads them again. Projects with node_modules keep working.
cat.bun.effect: Deletes the packages Bun kept in its cache; existing node_modules are not touched. The next bun install downloads whatever is missing again, with a connection and more time. If your projects link these files, the space actually recovered will be less than shown.
cat.deno.effect: Deletes the modules and packages Deno downloaded and its compiled code; localStorage and Deno KV data are kept. The next time you run a program, Deno downloads again what it uses, so it needs a connection and takes longer to start.
cat.playwright.effect: Deletes the browsers Playwright downloaded. Your tests will fail with a missing browser error until you reinstall them. They do not come back by themselves: run npx playwright install in your project.
cat.node-projects.effect: Deletes the node_modules, .next or .nuxt folders you choose. The project will not start or build until you reinstall its dependencies with npm install (or pnpm install, yarn install or bun install, depending on the project). The .next and .nuxt folders are created again on the next build.
cat.pip.effect: Deletes the packages pip kept in its cache; what you already installed is not touched. The next pip install downloads again what it needs, with a connection and more time.
cat.uv.effect: Deletes the uv cache; existing virtual environments keep working. The next uv sync, uv pip install or uv run downloads whatever is missing again, with a connection and more time. If your projects link these files, the space actually recovered will be less than shown.
cat.poetry.effect: Deletes the packages Poetry kept in its cache; the virtual environments Poetry manages are kept. The next poetry install downloads whatever is missing again, with a connection and more time.
cat.python-projects.effect: Deletes the virtual environments and the __pycache__ or .pytest_cache folders you choose. A project without its environment will not run until you create it again and install its dependencies (python -m venv .venv and pip install, or uv sync or poetry install). The __pycache__ and .pytest_cache folders come back by themselves when you run the code or the tests.
cat.go-build.effect: Deletes the results of earlier Go builds. The next go build or go test compiles everything again and takes longer. You do not have to do anything: Go creates them again.
cat.go-mod.effect: Deletes the modules Go downloaded. The next build downloads them again (or go mod download), with a connection and more time; private modules will need your usual access.
cat.cargo.effect: Deletes the crates and git repositories Cargo downloaded; programs installed with cargo install are not touched. The next cargo build downloads them again, with a connection and more time.
cat.rust-target.effect: Deletes the target folders you choose, with the build output and executables of those projects. The next cargo build compiles everything from scratch, which can take several minutes.
cat.gradle.effect: Deletes the downloaded dependencies and build output Gradle keeps in its cache. The next build downloads and generates them again, with a connection and more time.
cat.maven.effect: Deletes the local Maven repository. The next build downloads the public dependencies again, with a connection and more time. What you installed yourself with mvn install is not on any server: you have to run mvn install again in those projects.
cat.nuget.effect: Deletes the downloaded .NET packages and the NuGet download cache. The next dotnet restore or build downloads them again, with a connection and more time.
cat.composer.effect: Deletes the packages Composer kept in its cache; the vendor folders of your projects are not touched. The next composer install downloads whatever is missing again, with a connection and more time.
cat.dart-pub.effect: Deletes the Dart and Flutter packages pub downloaded. Projects that use them will not build until you run dart pub get or flutter pub get, which downloads them again with a connection.
cat.cpp.effect: Deletes the binary packages kept by vcpkg and Conan. When a project asks for them, they are downloaded or compiled again, which can take a long time. Conan packages you created yourself with conan create are not on any server: you have to create them again.
cat.zig.effect: Deletes the global Zig cache, with build output and downloaded packages. The next zig build downloads the packages again and compiles from scratch, with a connection and more time.
cat.terraform-projects.effect: Deletes the .terraform folders you choose, with the downloaded providers and modules; your state (terraform.tfstate) is not there and is not touched. terraform plan and apply will fail until you run terraform init again, with the same -backend-config options if you used them. If you were working in another workspace, select it again with terraform workspace select.
cat.git-worktrees.effect: Removes the folder of each chosen worktree and its record in git; the branch and its commits are kept in the repository. A Claude session that worked in it will not be able to continue there. If you need it again, create it with git worktree add followed by a path and the branch.
cat.web-testing.effect: Deletes the programs Cypress and Puppeteer downloaded. Your tests will fail until you reinstall them. They do not come back by themselves: run npx cypress install or npx puppeteer browsers install in your project.
cat.native-build.effect: Deletes the Electron binaries kept for installing and packaging apps. The next install or packaging run downloads them again, with a connection and more time.
cat.vscode.effect: Deletes the VS Code caches; your settings, extensions and projects are not touched. Anything in use while the editor is open is skipped, and it may take a little longer to open next time. VS Code creates them again by itself.
cat.jetbrains.effect: Deletes the caches folders of the JetBrains IDEs; your settings and plugins are not there. When you open each project, the IDE rebuilds what it needs, which can take several minutes.
cat.huggingface.effect: Deletes the models and datasets downloaded from Hugging Face; your access token is kept. The next program that uses them downloads them again, which can take a long time with large models and does not work offline.
cat.minikube.effect: Deletes the Minikube cache, with downloaded images and binaries; your clusters are not touched. The next minikube start downloads whatever is missing again, with a connection and more time.
cat.antigravity-cache.effect: Deletes the Antigravity caches; your settings and projects are not touched. It may take a little longer to open next time. Antigravity creates them again by itself.
cat.claude-sessions.effect: Deletes the contents of the session temporary folders you choose; those with recent activity are skipped. Files left in those folders, including ones you asked Claude to leave there, are lost and do not come back. Your conversations are stored elsewhere and are not touched; Claude creates the folder again when it needs it.
cat.docker.effect: Clean removes stopped containers, unused networks, untagged images and unused build cache; anything inside a stopped container that is not in a volume is lost, and volumes are not touched, although the anonymous volume of a removed container is left orphaned: a new container will not reattach it. With "All unused images" it also removes every image no container uses and all build cache: you will have to download it with docker pull or build it with docker build again. Compact does not delete data, but it stops Docker and every WSL distribution while it runs, and its method is not officially documented.
cat.podman.effect: Clean removes stopped containers, unused pods, unused networks and untagged images; anything inside a stopped container that is not in a volume is lost, and volumes are not touched, although the anonymous volume of a removed container is left orphaned: a new container will not reattach it. With "All unused images" it also removes every image no container uses: you will have to download it with podman pull or build it with podman build again. Compact does not delete data, but it stops the Podman machine and every WSL distribution while it runs, and its method is not officially documented.
terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lead: Before deleting anything with Limpyrid, read and accept these terms. Summary of TERMINOS.md:
terms.point.1: Limpyrid deletes files and folders from your computer. Most cleanups are permanent: what is deleted does not go to the Recycle Bin and cannot be recovered from the app.
terms.point.2: You decide what is cleaned and you are responsible for what you select. The app shows what it will delete and asks you to confirm; by confirming, you accept that deletion.
terms.point.3: The app's protections reduce the risk of deleting something you need, but do not remove it. Keep backups of anything you care about.
terms.point.4: Limpyrid is provided as is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied.
terms.point.5: To the extent permitted by law, Pergamio and contributors are not liable for any damage arising from its use, including loss of data, unsaved work, time or income.
